paper_a.title: Exact Recovery in the Stochastic Block Model

metadata.description: Stochastic Block Model exact-recovery (Abbe-Bandeira-Hall, sparse random-graph community detection, sharp information-theoretic threshold via ML / SDP / Matrix Bernstein) vs Denoising Diffusion Probabilistic Models (Ho-Jain-Abbeel, continuous-state Gaussian Markov-chain generative model trained by a variational ELBO and a noise-prediction MSE). The two papers share at most the abstract notion 'stochastic model'. Their objects (sparse 2-block random graph vs Gaussian diffusion latent-variable model), their target tasks (combinatorial community recovery vs image generation / density modelling), their proof techniques (binomial-difference tail bounds, Matrix Bernstein, KKT/SDP duality vs ELBO derivations, Gaussian-KL Rao-Blackwellisation, reparameterisation tricks), and their algorithms (ML / SDP / partial-recovery+local-flip vs SGD training of a noise predictor and ancestral Langevin-like sampling) have no meaningful node-level correspondence. No exact or analogous matches were found after honest inspection.

matches.explanation: Stochastic Block Model G(n,p,q) is a discrete random-graph model with two equal-sized communities and Bernoulli edges. DDPM has no random-graph object, no community structure, and no Bernoulli edge model; its 'stochastic process' is a continuous Gaussian Markov chain over Euclidean image space.

Exact recovery of a planted bipartition (probability of recovering the true labels tends to 1) has no counterpart in DDPM, which is concerned with sample quality, log-likelihood, and rate-distortion, not recovery of a hidden discrete structure.

Auxiliary failure events F, F_A, Delta, F_H^{(j)}, F_H are bookkeeping for the SBM information-theoretic lower bound. DDPM has no analogue: there are no failure events, no min-bisection-style decoder, and no probability-of-error analysis of a discrete decoder.

Tail function T(N,p,q,eps) for the difference of two independent binomials is specific to the SBM's combinatorial concentration analysis. DDPM uses Gaussian KL divergences and Jensen's inequality; no binomial-difference tail appears.
The signed SBM Laplacian L_{SBM} = D^+ - D^- - A is a graph operator built from within-/across-community degrees. DDPM has no graph, no Laplacian, no spectral object of this kind.
Dominant binomial term T*(m,p,q,eps) is an analytic device for sharpening the SBM tail bound. No analogous binomial saddle-point quantity occurs in DDPM.

Maximum-likelihood / min-bisection of a graph is an NP-hard combinatorial optimisation problem. DDPM's optimisation problem is a continuous variational-bound minimisation; no min-bisection or balanced cut appears.
Combinatorial +/-1 quadratic max_x x^T B x is the spin-glass-style reformulation of min-bisection. DDPM has no such Boolean quadratic problem.
SDP relaxation max_{X >= 0, X_ii = 1} Tr(BX) is a Goemans-Williamson-style convex relaxation. DDPM does not relax to an SDP and does not solve a convex matrix optimisation problem.

Recovery threshold (alpha+beta)/2 - sqrt(alpha*beta) > 1 is a sharp phase-transition formula specific to two-community SBM in the log-degree regime. DDPM has no phase transition or sharp threshold of this form.
PSD/eigenvalue dual-feasibility condition 2 L_{SBM} + I_n - 11^T >= 0 with lambda_2 > 0 is an SDP-uniqueness certificate. DDPM has no SDP and no dual certificate.

Information-theoretic lower bound for SBM exact recovery (impossibility below the (alpha+beta)/2 - sqrt(alpha*beta) = 1 line) is a converse phase-transition theorem. DDPM has no impossibility theorem of this character; its main results are derivations and empirical sample-quality numbers.

Achievability of exact recovery by ML above the same threshold has no DDPM counterpart. The Ho-Jain-Abbeel paper proves no recovery / phase-transition theorem; its formal results are algebraic identities for the variational bound.

SDP recovery guarantee (uniqueness of gg^T as the SDP optimum under (alpha-beta)^2 > 8(alpha+beta) + 8(alpha-beta)/3) is a polynomial-time achievability result for community recovery. DDPM has no convex-optimisation guarantee.
Threshold-achieving partition-then-local-flip algorithm for SBM is a graph-algorithmic result. DDPM is a generative-modelling paper with no two-stage combinatorial recovery procedure.
Lemma converting P(F_A) >= 2/3 to P(F) >= 1/3 is internal SBM-failure bookkeeping. No analogous lemma in DDPM.
Reverse union bound on F_H is internal SBM-failure bookkeeping. No analogue in DDPM.
Reduction to per-node failure probability rho(n) is specific to the SBM ML-failure proof. No analogous reduction in DDPM.
Asymptotic bound on -log T (binomial-difference log-tail) provides the sharp SBM exponent. DDPM uses no binomial-tail asymptotic.
Combinatorial witness lemma (ML failure implies a balanced swap of equal-size subsets). No combinatorial swap argument in DDPM.
Bernstein-style upper bound on the binomial-difference tail used in the ML-success proof. DDPM does not use Bernstein-type concentration.
Two-sided dominant-term bounds via the function g(alpha,beta,epsilon) are an analytic refinement of binomial concentration specific to SBM. No such function appears in DDPM.
Mislabel-probability upper bound for the partition-then-local-flip algorithm. DDPM has no node-level mislabel probability.
Bound P(Delta) >= 9/10 on max-degree of a small auxiliary subgraph. DDPM has no graph and no degree.
KKT/dual sufficient condition for the SDP to recover gg^T. DDPM has no KKT analysis and no convex relaxation.
Reduction of SDP success to two spectral-tail bounds on Gamma. No spectral matrix-tail analysis appears in DDPM.
Tail bound for the projection of Gamma onto span(1) via Matrix Bernstein. DDPM does not invoke Matrix Bernstein.
Tail bound for the orthogonal-to-1 projection of Gamma; the threshold-achieving step of the SDP proof. No counterpart in DDPM.
Uniform degree bound on H_1 nodes used to split edges between G_1 and G_2. DDPM has no edge split.

SDP-based community recovery algorithm. DDPM's algorithms are SGD training (AP12.1), ancestral sampling (AP12.2), and progressive-coding sender/receiver (AP12.3-4); none is a convex relaxation of a combinatorial cut.
Two-stage partial-recovery + local-flip algorithm for SBM. DDPM has no two-stage recovery procedure; its algorithms operate on continuous Gaussian states, not graphs.

Maximum-likelihood / min-bisection decoder. DDPM does not use a maximum-likelihood decoder of any combinatorial structure; training optimises a variational upper bound on negative log-likelihood, which is a different object.
Proof of SBM lower bound via per-node failure probability. DDPM proofs (PP12.1-3) are algebraic ELBO manipulations; no probabilistic-impossibility argument.
Proof of SBM upper bound via union bound over swap subsets and Bernstein-style binomial-difference bound. DDPM uses no union-bound-over-combinatorial-subsets argument.
Proof of SDP guarantee via KKT + Matrix Bernstein on Gamma. DDPM has no convex-duality + spectral-concentration proof.
Proof of efficient threshold-achieving algorithm via random edge split + per-node mislabel bound + union bound. No structurally similar proof in DDPM.
Open question on whether SDP/spectral algorithms attain the IT recovery threshold. DDPM lists no open problems of this kind.
Open question relating detection and recovery thresholds in SBM. No DDPM counterpart.
Open question on extending sharp threshold to multi-community / overlapping / labelled SBMs. No DDPM counterpart.

Diffusion model as a latent-variable model p_theta(x_0) = integral p_theta(x_{0:T}) dx_{1:T}. SBM has no latent-variable generative model; its 'latents' are the discrete labels X_v, which are inferred not integrated out, and the model is over a discrete random graph.
Reverse process: a learned Gaussian Markov chain with neural-network mean / covariance. SBM has no Markov chain over data, no learned Gaussian transitions, and no neural network.
Forward Gaussian-noise diffusion process. SBM has no continuous-time / discrete-time noising of data; its randomness is a single i.i.d. draw of Bernoulli edges.
Cumulative noise-schedule notation alpha_t, bar-alpha_t. No noise schedule appears in SBM.
Discrete pixel decoder built by integrating a Gaussian over 1/255 bins. SBM has no decoder of this kind; its 'decoder' (the ML estimator) acts on a graph and outputs a partition.
Simplified noise-prediction MSE training objective L_simple. SBM has no noise-prediction loss; in fact SBM has no training objective at all, since its decoders are not learned.
Variational ELBO upper bound on negative log-likelihood. SBM uses no variational inference and no ELBO; its likelihood analysis works directly with the joint Bernoulli graph distribution.
Closed-form Gaussian marginal q(x_t|x_0). SBM has no Gaussian marginal of this kind; its closed-form quantities are binomial probabilities of edge counts.
Decomposed KL form of the variational bound (L_T + sum L_{t-1} + L_0). No telescoping KL decomposition in SBM.
Forward-posterior Gaussian q(x_{t-1}|x_t,x_0) with closed-form mean and variance. No Gaussian posterior of this kind in SBM.
Reverse-mean parameterisation through a noise-prediction network epsilon_theta. No neural-network parameterisation in SBM.
Denoising-score-matching form of L_{t-1}. SBM has no score-matching objective.
Rate-distortion form of the variational bound. SBM uses no rate-distortion decomposition.
Progressive estimate hat-x_0 = (x_t - sqrt(1-bar-alpha_t) epsilon_theta) / sqrt(bar-alpha_t). SBM has no progressive denoising estimator.
SGD training of a noise-prediction network. SBM contains no learning algorithm; its decoders (ML / SDP / partial-recovery+flip) are non-parametric and require no training.

Ancestral Langevin-like sampling from the trained reverse process. SBM has no sampling algorithm of this kind; AP3.1 / AP3.2 / AP3.4 all extract a single combinatorial partition rather than draw continuous samples.
Progressive-coding sender (minimal random coding). SBM has no compression / coding algorithm.
Progressive-coding receiver. No counterpart in SBM.

Likelihood-based training of a parametric generative model via ELBO minimisation. SBM does not train a parametric model; its problem is to recover a hidden discrete structure from a single sampled graph.
Image generation via simulating the reverse Markov chain. SBM has no generative simulation problem.
Progressive lossy compression of x_0. No compression problem in SBM.
Derivation of decomposed ELBO via Bayes' rule + telescoping. SBM proofs do not telescope a variational bound; they perform binomial-tail and matrix-Bernstein analyses.
Reduction of L_{t-1} to noise-prediction MSE via reparameterisation. No reparameterisation-trick proof in SBM.
Derivation of the rate-distortion form of the variational bound. SBM has no rate-distortion derivation.
